questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusion numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide 

Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All creepers are vegetables.

All vegetables are fruits.

Some fruits are flowers.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some creepers are flowers.

II. Some fruits are creepers.

III. All vegetables are flowers.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusion I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

All creepers are vegetables.

All vegetables are fruits.

Some fruits are flowers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e6830d7181033d85781aec13e41455565739755b95e8a7ae77f873e1a758d90.png] 

__**Conclusions**__**:**

I. Some creepers are flowers → Does not follow → We have no information which suggests the relationship between creepers and flowers so we cannot assume anything and thus the conclusion does not follow.

II. Some fruits are creepers→ Follow → Since all creepers are fruits, they both are directly related to each other & the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so we can say that some fruits are creepers therefore the conclusion follows.

III. All vegetables are flowers→ Does not follow → We have 'All vegetables are fruits' and 'Some fruits are flowers' which means vegetables and flowers are directly not related to each other so the conclusion does not follow.

So **only conclusion II follows.**

Hence,** the correct answer is option 2).**

questions.question: What is the name of the Gulf that separates Finland and Sweden
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulf of Bothnia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Gulf of Bothnia**

 
 
• It is the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea, separating Finland and Sweden.
 
• The gulf freezes over in winter, creating unique ice conditions for shipping and ecosystems.
 
• Major ports along its coast include Umeå (Sweden) and Vaasa (Finland).
 
• It is known for its archipelago landscapes and brackish water with low salinity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Gulf of Genoa**

 
 
• Gulf of Genoa is located in the Mediterranean Sea, not the Baltic.
 
• It lies along the northwestern coast of Italy, near the region of Liguria.
 
• The city of Genoa, a major Italian port, sits at its center.
 
• This gulf is known for its deep waters and importance in Mediterranean trade.
 
• It has no geographical connection to Scandinavia or the Baltic region.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Riga**
 
 
• Gulf of Riga is part of the Baltic Sea but does not separate Finland and Sweden.
 
• It is situated between Latvia and Estonia, with Riga (Latvia's capital) on its coast.
 
• The gulf is relatively shallow and freezes partially in winter.
 
• It is an important fishing area, especially for herring and flounder.
 
• Unlike the Gulf of Bothnia, it lies much farther south in the Baltic region.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Gdansk**
 
 
• Gulf of Gdansk is another Baltic Sea inlet but unrelated to Finland or Sweden.
 
• Located along Poland's northern coast, it includes the port city of Gdańsk.
 
• It is known for its shipyards, maritime history, and amber trade.
 
• The Vistula River delta empties into this gulf, creating unique wetland ecosystems.
 
• It lies south of the Gulf of Bothnia and does not border any Scandinavian countries.

questions.question: Cream is separated from milk during churning due to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**centrifugal force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

 
• **Centrifugal force**

 
 
• Cream is separated from milk during churning primarily due to centrifugal force.
 
• Churning involves rotating the milk at high speeds, causing denser components (like skim milk) to move outward.
 
• Lighter fat globules (cream) cluster together and separate from the liquid due to this outward force.
 
• This process mimics industrial centrifugal separators used in dairy production.
 
• Centrifugal force is a pseudo-force that appears in rotating frames of reference.
 
• Unlike gravity, it efficiently separates immiscible liquids of different densities.
 
• Traditional churning uses this principle by agitating milk until fat coalesces into butter or cream.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force**
 
 
• Gravity acts downward but is too weak alone to separate cream efficiently.
 
• Cream naturally rises over time due to density differences, but this is slow (taking hours or days).
 
• Industrial separation relies on centrifugal force to accelerate this process.
 
• Gravity's role is minimal in mechanical churning or centrifugation.
 
• Sedimentation due to gravity is impractical for large-scale dairy processing.
 
• Centrifugal force in machines provides faster, more controlled separation.
 
• Thus, gravity is not the primary force in churning.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Force**
 
 
• Friction occurs between milk particles and container walls during churning.
 
• However, it does not directly contribute to cream separation.
 
• Frictional heat may slightly affect viscosity but doesn't aid in fat globule clustering.
 
• The key separation mechanism is density-based, not friction-dependent.
 
• In butter-making, friction helps clump fat after separation, but not in initial cream extraction.
 
• Industrial separators minimize friction to allow smooth rotation.
 
• Thus, frictional force is irrelevant to the core separation process.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force**
 
 
• Centripetal force acts inward, keeping milk particles in circular motion during churning.
 
• It is the real force (provided by container walls) that enables rotation.
 
• However, it does not cause separation—centrifugal force (outward effect) does.
 
• Separation occurs because denser components resist motion more, moving outward.
 
• Centripetal force is necessary for rotation but not the direct cause of cream separation.

questions.question: Under flexible exchange rate, when the price of domestic currency in terms of foreign currency increases, it is called ___________ .
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - Appreciation of domestic currency**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Appreciation of domestic currency**

 
 
• Under a flexible exchange rate system, currencies fluctuate based on market forces of demand and supply.
 
• When the price of domestic currency in terms of foreign currency increases, it means that the domestic currency has become stronger or more valuable relative to the foreign currency.
 
• This increase in value is referred to as an appreciation of the domestic currency.
 
• For instance, if the exchange rate changes from 1 USD = 70 INR to 1 USD = 65 INR, the Indian Rupee (INR) has appreciated.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Depreciation of domestic currency**

 
 
• Depreciation refers to a decrease in the value of the domestic currency relative to foreign currencies under a flexible exchange rate system.
 
• It occurs due to market forces such as changes in demand and supply, economic conditions, or geopolitical events.
 
 
 
• **Devaluation of domestic currency**
 
 
• Devaluation is a deliberate downward adjustment to the value of a country's currency relative to another currency or a standard under a fixed exchange rate system.
 
• It is often implemented by a country's government or monetary authority to correct imbalances.
 
 
 
• **Revaluation of domestic currency**
 
 
• Revaluation is the opposite of devaluation, where the value of the currency is increased by the government or monetary authority under a fixed exchange rate system.
 
• This action makes the currency stronger in relation to foreign currencies.

questions.question: Which one among the following is an example of chemical change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixing of NaOH and HCl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mixing of NaOH (sodium hydroxide) and HCl (hydrochloric acid) results in a chemical reaction.
 
• This reaction is an example of a neutralization reaction, where an acid reacts with a base to produce a salt and water.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O.
 
• In this process, new substances (sodium chloride and water) are formed, indicating a chemical change.
 
• Energy is usually released in the form of heat during this exothermic reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Change**

 
 
• A chemical change results in the formation of one or more new substances with different properties.
 
• Indicators of a chemical change include color change, temperature change, gas production, and the formation of a precipitate.
 
• Examples include rusting of iron, burning of wood, and baking a cake.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**
 
 
• A neutralization reaction occurs when an acid and a base react to form water and a salt.
 
• These reactions are typically exothermic, releasing heat.
 
• Neutralization reactions are important in various industrial processes, laboratory experiments, and even in everyday life, such as in antacid tablets neutralizing stomach acid.
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction**
 
 
• An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases energy through light or heat.
 
• Common examples include combustion reactions and many oxidation reactions.
 
• Exothermic reactions are characterized by an increase in the temperature of the surroundings.
 
 
 
• **Balanced Chemical Equation**
 
 
• A balanced chemical equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the equation.
 
• Balancing equations is essential to follow the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• Balancing equations ensures that the chemical process is accurately represented.

__
 
• **Central Bank**

 
 
• The Central Bank is the primary monetary authority of a country, often responsible for implementing monetary policy, issuing currency, and overseeing the financial system.
 
• While commercial banks accept deposits and give loans to individuals and businesses, the Central Bank does not engage in these activities directly with the public.
 
• Instead, the Central Bank regulates and supervises commercial banks to ensure the stability and efficiency of the financial system.

• **Banker to the Government**
 
 
• The Central Bank acts as a banker to the government by managing its accounts, facilitating transactions, and providing short-term funding.
 
• It also advises the government on economic and financial matters.
 
 
 
• **Issuance of Currency**
 
 
• The Central Bank has the sole authority to issue currency notes and coins in the country.
 
• This ensures a uniform and controlled supply of money, reducing the risk of counterfeiting and maintaining public confidence in the currency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Granite** is primarily an igneous rock, formed from the slow crystallization of magma beneath the Earth's surface.
 
• It is composed mainly of quartz, feldspar, and mica minerals, giving it a granular texture.
 
• Granite can undergo metamorphism, transforming into a metamorphic rock known as gneiss when subjected to high pressure and temperature conditions.
 
• During the metamorphic process, the mineral composition of granite may realign to form new structures, but the original minerals may still be identifiable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Examples include basalt, granite, and pumice.
 
• Classified into intrusive (plutonic) and extrusive (volcanic) types.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks:**
 
 
• Formed from the alteration of existing rock types in the Earth's crust due to heat, pressure, and chemically active fluids.
 
• Examples include gneiss, schist, and marble.
 
• Two main types: foliated (with a layered appearance) and non-foliated (without a layered appearance).
 
 
 
• **Formation of Gneiss:**
 
 
• Gneiss is a high-grade metamorphic rock formed from pre-existing rocks like granite, shale, or volcanic rocks.
 
• Characterized by its banded texture resulting from the segregation of mineral layers.
 
 
 
• **Geological Significance:**
 
 
• Granite is widely used in construction due to its durability and aesthetic appeal.
 
• Metamorphic rocks like gneiss provide insights into the geological processes and conditions within the Earth's crust.

questions.question: The AC mains domestic supply current in India changes direction in every
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**AC Mains Supply Frequency**

__
 
• Alternating Current (AC) in domestic power supply means the current changes direction periodically.
 
• The frequency of the AC mains supply in India is 50 Hz.
 
• One complete cycle of AC means it goes from positive to negative and back to positive.
 
• The time period (T) of one complete cycle is the reciprocal of the frequency (f).

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• Given the frequency (f) of AC mains supply in India is 50 Hz:
 
 
• Time period (T) = 1 / f
 
• = 1 / 50 seconds
 
• = 0.02 seconds
 
 
 
• Since the current changes direction twice in each cycle (once every half cycle):
 
 
• The direction changes every T/2 seconds
 
• = 0.02 / 2 seconds
 
• = 0.01 seconds
 
• = 1/100 seconds
 
 

**Therefore, the AC mains domestic supply current in India changes direction in every 1/100 seconds.**

• Tropical grasslands, known as savannas, are found in warm climates with distinct wet and dry seasons.

• Dominant trees include spruce, pine, and fir, adapted to snowy conditions.
 
• Wildlife includes moose, wolves, and bears, unlike the open grasslands of savannas.
 
 
 
• **Pampas**

• Located in South America (Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil), they have fertile soils ideal for agriculture.
 
• These grasslands experience moderate rainfall and no extreme temperatures.

questions.question: If I am suffering from thyroid problems, I need to consult a ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Endocrinologist**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Endocrinologist

 
 
• An endocrinologist specializes in diagnosing and treating hormone-related disorders, including thyroid problems.
 
• The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate metabolism, making endocrinologists the right experts for thyroid issues.
 
• They treat conditions like hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Hashimoto’s disease, and Graves' disease.
 
• Endocrinologists perform blood tests (TSH, T3, T4) and imaging (ultrasound, radioactive iodine scans) for diagnosis.
 
• They prescribe medications (levothyroxine, methimazole) or recommend treatments like radioactive iodine therapy or surgery.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diabetologist**

 
 
• A diabetologist focuses on diabetes mellitus (Type 1, Type 2, and gestational diabetes).
 
• While diabetes is a hormonal disorder, diabetologists do not primarily treat thyroid conditions.
 
• Some endocrinologists also specialize in diabetes, but a pure diabetologist may not handle thyroid cases.
 
• Thyroid issues can affect blood sugar, but management requires an endocrinologist, not just a diabetologist.
 
• Patients with both diabetes and thyroid disorders should see an endocrinologist for comprehensive care.
 
 
 
• **Oncologist**
 
 
• An oncologist specializes in diagnosing and treating cancer, including thyroid cancer.
 
• However, most thyroid problems (like hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism) are not cancerous.
 
• If a thyroid nodule is suspected to be malignant, an endocrinologist may refer the patient to an oncologist.
 
• Routine thyroid disorders (non-cancerous) do not require an oncologist’s expertise.
 
• Only in rare cases of thyroid cancer would an oncologist (or endocrine surgeon) be involved.
 
 
 
• **Ophthalmologist**
 
 
• An ophthalmologist is an eye doctor who diagnoses and treats eye diseases and vision problems.
 
• Some thyroid disorders (like Graves' disease) can cause eye symptoms (bulging eyes, dryness, double vision).
 
• In such cases, an endocrinologist may collaborate with an ophthalmologist for eye-related complications.
 
• However, an ophthalmologist alone cannot diagnose or treat thyroid hormone imbalances.
 
• Thyroid-related eye disease (TED) requires both an endocrinologist and an ophthalmologist for full management

• Kushanas issued mostly gold coins and numerous copper coins which have been found in most parts of North India up to Bihar.
 
• The **Gold Dinara's or Suvarnas** were based on the ***Roman denarius*** and were of 124 grains (8.04 grams).
 
 
• Double and quarter Dinaras were also issued. The copper coins were large, from 26 to 28 Masas or 240 to 260 grains (15.55 to 16.85) grams.
 
 
 
• The coins of ***Vima Kadphises*** bear the figure of **Siva standing beside a bull.**
 
• In the legend on these coins, the king calls himself ***Maheshwara***, i.e. devotee of Siva.
 
 
• Kanishka, Huvishka and Vasudeva etc. all have this depiction on their coins.
 
 
 
• Many Indian gods and goddesses are depicted on Kushana coins besides many **Persian and Greek deities.**

questions.question: If the price of sugar surges by 25%, what percentage of the consumer's usage should fall if the expenditure remains constant?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the percentage increase into a fraction: 25% = +1/4.

To keep the expenditure constant, the consumption must decrease by the fraction: −1 ÷ (4 + 1).

Required decrease fraction = −1/5.

Percentage decrease in consumption = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of sugar surges (increases) by 25%.

Overall expenditure of the consumer remains constant.

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15c48d79be2a3f78f06444fd94210a136083b0a003a8b76def5eed5371d24671.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price of sugar be ₹100 per kg and the original consumption be 100 kg.

⇒ Original Expenditure = Price × Consumption = 100 × 100 = ₹10,000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 25% of 100 = ₹125 per kg.

⇒ Since the expenditure remains constant, New Expenditure = ₹10,000

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price = 10000 ÷ 125 = 80 kg.

⇒ Fall in consumption = Original Consumption − New Consumption = 100 − 80 = 20 kg.

⇒ Percentage fall in consumption = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Expenditure Concept

If Total Expenditure is constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional to each other, mathematically written as P₁ × C₁ = P₂ × C₂.

Price Reduction Rule

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, the consumption must be increased by (R ÷ (100 − R)) × 100% to maintain constant expenditure.

AB Rule for Percentage

If quantity A is x% more than quantity B, then B is (x ÷ (100 + x)) × 100% less than A. This direct formula approach saves computation time in ratio-based percentage questions.

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total members × Change in average)

Weight of girl = 80 + (60 × (−0.5))

Weight of girl = 80 − 30 = 50 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

Total students = 60

Average weight decrease = 0.5 kg

New Entry Weight = Replaced Weight + (Total Count × Average Change)

 Class (60 Students)

• Girl Joins (x kg) Net Change = 60 × (−0.5) = −30 kg 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial average weight of the class be A kg.

⇒ Total initial weight = 60 × A

⇒ After boy leaves and girl joins, new average = (A − 0.5) kg

⇒ Total new weight = 60 × (A − 0.5)

⇒ Total new weight = 60A − 30

⇒ Also, Total new weight = (Initial total − Boy weight + Girl weight)

⇒ 60A − 30 = 60A − 80 + Weight of girl

⇒ Weight of girl = 80 − 30

⇒ Weight of girl = 50 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

Total Change = (Number of observations) × (Change in Average). This is the fastest way to solve replacement problems.

questions.question: A man divided an amount between his sons in the ratio of their ages. The sons received Rs. 54000 and Rs. 48000. If one son is 5 years older than the other, find the age of the younger son.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of their ages = Ratio of amounts received = 54000 : 48000 = 9 : 8

Difference in ratio parts = 9 − 8 = 1 part

Since one son is 5 years older, 1 part = 5 years

Age of the younger son = 8 parts = 8 × 5 = 40 years

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount received by the older son = Rs. 54000

Amount received by the younger son = Rs. 48000

Age difference between the sons = 5 years

**Concept Used:**

When an amount is divided in the ratio of ages, the ratio of amounts equals the ratio of ages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fb7383922d72fd809cdee5929c952d38fb2f46a3e3bdd0d06d843791ad98273.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of ages = Ratio of amounts received

⇒ Ratio of ages = 54000 ÷ 48000 = 9 : 8

⇒ Let the age of the older son be 9x and the younger son be 8x.

⇒ Difference in ages = 9x − 8x = x

⇒ Given that the difference is 5 years, x = 5

⇒ Age of the younger son = 8x = 8 × 5 = 40 years

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportional Division

When a quantity Q is divided in the ratio a : b, the individual parts are (a / (a + b)) × Q and (b / (a + b)) × Q.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons remains perfectly constant throughout their lives, regardless of the number of years passed.

Direct Proportion
